newsitem.title: USA: Weekend freeze seen damaging US plains wheat - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Weekend freeze seen damaging US plains wheat - WSC.

text.p: Freezing temperatures in Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas over the weekend are seen damaging the developing U.S. hard red winter crop, a U.S. meteorologist said.
"It looks to be a very serious event in terms of loss of production to the central Plains winter wheat crop," said Joel Burgio, senior meteorologist with Weather Services Corp in Lexington, Mass.
On Saturday, temperatures dipped to five degrees Fahrenheit in Goodland, Kan., 10 degrees at Garden City, and 14 at Dodge City.
Lows in Gauge, Okla. dropped to 20 on Saturday, Enid, Okla. was 25 and Amarillo, Tex. fell to 17, Burgio said.
At this stage of growth for winter wheat, temperatures below 20 degrees can start to cause damage to wheat plants which are just forming new leaves.
Temperatures on Sunday throughout much of the central and southern Plains remained low enough to cause damage to the crop, Burgio said.
"The damage occurred on Saturday and Sunday," Burgio said. "We had a very serious freeze on those two mornings."
On Sunday, temperatures in Wichita, Kan. fell to 22 degrees, Enid, Okla. was 25 degrees, Oklahoma City was 26, Abilene, Texas fell to 29, and Amarillo was 23 degrees, Burgio said.
Temperatures are expected to warm toward more normal levels by the middle of this week, Burgio said.
"Temperatures are forecast below normal both today (Monday) and Tuesday, and then near normal Wednesday, so we are warming towards normal over the next several days," Burgio said.
